newsitem.title: UK: Enterprise /BP say in North Sea swap.
newsitem.headline: Enterprise /BP say in North Sea swap.

text.p: Enterprise Oil Plc and British Petroleum Co Plc said on Monday they had agreed a major asset trade involving interest in three North Sea fields.

Under the agreement, which is expected to be concluded soon, Enterprise will receive BP's 42.79 percent interest in the Pierce Field in exchange for 24.05 percent of the Amethyst gas field and 13.50 percent in the Ravenspurn North gas field.
The agreement is subject to the consent of the government and co-venturers.

Development is underway on Pierce which lies in Blocks 23/22a and 23/27 in the central North Sea. The project is expected to be given the go-ahead around the middle of this year with the first oil anticipated in the third quarter of 1998.

Enterprise already has a 31.20 percent interest in Pierce. Once the deal is completed, its share will rise to 73.99 percent and it is expected to become operator. Other participants include Ranger Oil with 15.60 percent.
"This is good news for both companies," said Enterprise technical director Mark Hope.

"Enterprise will be able to maximise the potential of Pierce through our experience in the central North Sea, while BP will be able to derive greater value from the assets in which they are already significant players."
BP will hold 45.40 percent as operator in Amethyst, located in Blocks 47/8a, 47/9a, 47/13a, 47/14a and 47/15a and producing gas since 1990.
BP will have a 33.50 percent stake in Ravenspurn North, located in Blocks 42.30 and 43.26 and producing gas since 1990. BHP is operator of Ravenspurn North with 18.00 percent.
